goal: A step session costs less quota and less wall-clock for the same work, and nothing that is doing work is killed. Measured 2026-09-05..12 over 155 step sessions (`scripts/measure-steps.py --since 2026-09-05 --until 2026-09-12 --min-turns 10`, and the per-session json under `~/mc/runner/log/`): every session ran on `claude-opus-5` at the machine's `effortLevel: high`, median 93 turns (p90 208), mean context per turn 112k tokens (cache_read / turns in `runs.tsv`; 36 sessions above 200k), median 7.7 USD at list price (p90 30.5, max 56.9), 258 sessions since 2026-09-04 at about 2 500 USD list. The Max 20x subscription includes every model, so the unit that matters is quota, and three sessions that week ended on `You've hit your weekly limit`.

Three things change, in this order. The prompt a step session gets carries its own step and the plan's frozen fields, not the whole `PLAN.json` (up to 115k characters today, `docs/project/sql-readiness/sql-w1-universe-closure/PLAN.json` in memoro), and the session runs with an auto-compact window so its context has a ceiling. The plan names the model, the effort and the advisor per step, with `sonnet` at `medium` effort advised by `opus` as the runner's default for a step (Martin, 2026-09-11: "Låt oss testa sonnet 5 medium som default med opus advisor.") — ruling 18 in `rulings.md`. And the wall-clock budget that killed a session at 90/120/180 minutes is gone: at a fixed interval the runner sends the running session a message asking it to judge whether the step can be finished, and only a session that has produced nothing at all for a long time is killed as stalled. (Martin, 2026-09-11: "Vi vill inte döda ett step som faktiskt gör ett arbete bara för att datorn laggar, tester tar lång tid, etc. Det enda som önskas är att en session avslutar sig själv om den kört fast.")

Since 2026-08-25 (`runs.tsv`): 15 step sessions were killed on the budget with no JSON and nothing landed (1 152 minutes), and 22 ended `plan-trespass`, each costing a repair session (1 027 minutes) — 18 % of all step minutes. The budget half is this project's; why trespass happens that often is not read yet and is not this project's.
contract: A step session is still one fresh headless session in one workarea, launched by `deps.session` in `src/mc/run.js` with the argument list `headlessArgs` builds in `src/mc/run-plan.js`. No other lane, no subagent orchestration by the runner.

The defaults for a step, unless the plan or the step says otherwise: model `sonnet`, effort `medium`, advisor `opus`. A repair session keeps `opus` with no effort flag. Brief, plan, helper and intake sessions are not touched by this project.

A plan overrides the defaults in `runner` (whole plan) and a step in its own `runner` (that step only); step wins over plan wins over default. Every key the schema accepts is one the runner reads — there is no field nothing enforces (`docs/project/README.md` § *The overall part*).

The frozen fields, the boundary check (`unauthorisedChanges` in `src/mc/plan-schema.js`) and what a step session may write do not change. A step's `runner` is written by the plan's author and is not the session's to change.
Nothing kills a session because of elapsed time alone. A session is killed only when it has written nothing to stdout for `stall_minutes`, and the row then says `stalled`.
What is measured stays measurable: `runs.tsv` keeps every column it has, in order, and gains columns only at the end; `scripts/measure-steps.py` keeps working on rows written before this project.
out_of_scope: Any change to memoro: its `AGENTS.md` (50k characters, loaded by every session in that repository), its test selection, its suites. What a memoro step runs is memoro's, and `npm test` there already selects affected tests.

Prompt-text rules about turns or test counts. Two were tried (`canon/roles/_common.md`, #576 and the step role's *verify what done_when names*) and the measurement of 2026-09-05..12 shows 0 multi-tool turns in 16 201 and a median of 6 test runs per session. This project changes what the runner does, not what it asks.
The plan-trespass rate, the gate, the merge lane, `mc brief`, and the page's layout beyond the one clock it draws for a running step.
Any per-step tool other than claude. `runner.tool` stays a plan-level key; a step on codex is not planned here.

Deciding the compaction window, the check-in interval and the stall limit for good. They are constants named in one place with the value this plan gives, and the measurement after twenty sessions is what settles them.

success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js`: `stepPrompt` for a three-step plan contains `steps[1]`'s `instruction` paragraphs and not `steps[0]`'s or `steps[2]`'s; the prompt for the largest plan on main today (`sql-w1-universe-closure`, memoro) is under 30k characters where it was 115k.

success_criteria.criterion: No session is killed on elapsed time. A session running past the check-in interval receives the check-in message and either goes on or ends itself with the step `blocked`; a session silent for the stall limit is killed and logged `stalled`.

Live: `~/mc/runner/log/<name>-<ts>.json` of a real step that ran past the interval contains the check-in as a user message in the transcript under `~/.claude/projects/`.

steps.title: The step prompt carries its own step, and the session's context has a ceiling
comments: `stepPrompt` takes the parsed `plan` and no longer `planText` — the parameter is dropped and the one caller (`run.js`, `plan: plan.plan`) fixed. The own step is rendered key by key from `Object.entries`, so the `runner` key step 2 adds to a step reaches the session with no change to the rendering. `headlessArgs` takes `autocompact` (default `AUTOCOMPACT_TOKENS`); `helper-turn.js` passes `autocompact: null`, because the contract leaves helper and intake sessions as they were. The repair session gets the window like a step.

Criterion 0 is left `met: false` on purpose. Measured 2026-09-11 against memoro's origin/main with the new `stepPrompt`: `sql-w1-universe-closure` has grown to 133 771 characters (the plan says 115k); the prompt for each of its 26 ready steps is 21.2k–23.8k characters, but its blocked `steps[7]` renders at 31.8k because that step's own `comments` are 10k, and the done steps 3 and 6 at 30.4k for the same reason. `msr-core/items-sweep` (133 965 characters) renders its ready `steps[7]` at 36.0k — 20k of that is the step's own comments. The floor of about 21k is the frozen fields and criteria (about 6.7k) plus 34 one-line steps (their `done_when` alone is 8.7k). Nothing more can be cut without dropping the own step's comments, which the instruction keeps in full. Whether that meets "under 30k" is the planning session's call.

Baseline for context per turn, the row `scripts/measure-steps.py` now prints, over `--since 2026-09-05 --until 2026-09-12 --min-turns 10` (159 sessions): median 108.7k tokens, p75 163.4k, p90 218.7k, max 297.3k.

Today the prompt ends with `----- PLAN.json -----` followed by `planText`, the entire file as read from `origin/main` (`run.js` about line 1740: `planText: plan.text`). The session has that same file on disk in its worktree and edits it there; the copy in the prompt is only for reading, and it is read on every turn because it is in the prompt. Replace `planText` in the prompt with a rendering built from the parsed plan. `stepPrompt` already receives `step` and `index`; give it the parsed `plan` object too (the caller has it: `plan.plan` beside `plan.text`), and keep `planText` accepted but unused for one release so nothing that still passes it breaks — or drop it and fix the one caller, your choice, but say which in the PR. The rendering, in this order, each part under a heading the session can search for: `goal`, `contract`, `out_of_scope`, `success_criteria` (index, `met`, criterion, check), `documents`, `runner` if present; then `Your step` — `steps[index]` in full, every field, `instruction` and `comments` as paragraphs; then `The other steps` — one line each: `steps[i] · <status> · <title> · done when: <done_when>`, with `pr` where it has one. Nothing else from the other steps: their instructions are what makes the prompt 30k tokens, and the session that needs one can read the file.

The paragraph that says *Below is your plan, `<planPath>`* stays true because the file is still at that path in the worktree; say instead that the plan is on disk at that path and that what follows is the part of it this step needs. The rule about what the session may edit (`status`, `pr`, `comments`, `met`) and the blocked route do not change.

Then the ceiling. `headlessArgs` (about line 693) builds the claude argument list; add `'--autocompact', String(AUTOCOMPACT_TOKENS)` for claude only (codex has no such flag), with `export const AUTOCOMPACT_TOKENS = 150_000` beside `DEFAULT_MODEL` and a comment saying why 150k: the mean context per turn over 2026-09-05..12 was 112k, 36 of 295 sessions averaged over 200k, and one over 300k; the window makes claude compact at 150k instead of near the model's limit. Confirmed 2026-09-11: `claude --help` on 2.1.268 lists `--autocompact <auto|tokens>` (100k–1M). It is a constant, not a plan field, because nothing has yet shown a plan needing a different one; the measurement after twenty sessions is where that would show.

`scripts/measure-steps.py` already prints turns and cost from the per-session json. Add one row, `context per turn (k tokens)`, computed per session as `cache_read_input_tokens + input_tokens` divided by `num_turns` from the session json (the same fields `readSessionOutput` writes into `runs.tsv`), with the same quantiles the other rows have. This is the number step 1 is measured on.

steps.title: Model, effort and advisor per step, with sonnet at medium advised by opus as the default
comments: `sessionSettings(planRunner, stepRunner, { kind })` resolves `model`, `effort` and `advisor` one key at a time, step over plan over `SESSION_DEFAULTS[kind]` (`run-plan.js`); `DEFAULT_MODEL` is gone. A repair gets the plan's `runner` but never a step's — in the plan lane it is a session on a pull request, and in the merge lane there is no plan at all, so it is `sessionSettings({}, null, { kind: 'repair' })`. Because keys resolve separately, this plan's own `runner: { model: 'opus' }` makes step 3 run on opus at medium with an opus advisor, not on sonnet.

`unauthorisedChanges` no longer skips the session's own step whole: it compares every key of it except `status`, `pr`, `comments` and `blocked_by` (`SESSION_STEP_FIELDS`, `plan-schema.js`), so a changed `runner`, `instruction` or `done_when` on the own step is a `plan-trespass`. On a step `runner`, `tool` and `budget_minutes` are refused as `a plan-level key` rather than `unknown key`.

runs.tsv on this machine still has its original thirteen-column header, so a reader keyed by the header (`close-workarea.js`, `brief-collect.js`) sees neither `land_seconds` nor `model`; `archive-plan.js` reads by position and stops at `note`. `model` is the model the runner asked for; `measure-steps.py` groups by the `modelUsage` key with the most output in each session's json, which is what the session actually ran on. Run over `--since 2026-09-10 --until 2026-09-12` it printed 7 sessions, all `main model claude-opus-5`.

Criterion 1 is left `met: false`: its check is a live `starting` line and a runs.tsv `model` cell matched against `modelUsage`, and no session has run on this code yet. The tests cover the resolution, the argument list through the real claude adapter, the starting line and the row. `--advisor` is not in `claude --help` on 2.1.268; the plan records it accepted on a one-turn `claude -p`, and this session did not run one. If a later claude drops it, every step fails on its argument list, and `runner: { advisor: 'off' }` in a plan is the way around it.

The workarea was handed over on `step-cost-2`, which had already landed as #693: `branchLanded` answers `unknown` when `git merge-tree` conflicts, so `freshBranch` did not move it, and the push-guard refused the push. It was pushed with `MC_PUSH_ANYWAY=1` and #695 opened from the same head, since the runner finds a project's PR by `--head <branch> --state open`. Written up as a proposal (`~/mc/proposals/2026-09-11-landed-branch-that-conflicts-is-not-moved.md`).
steps.done_when: `PLAN.json` accepts `effort` and `advisor` in `runner` and a `runner` object with `model`, `effort` and `advisor` on a step; `sessionSettings` resolves step over plan over default, the defaults for a step being `sonnet`, `medium`, `opus` and for a repair `opus` with no effort and no advisor; `headlessArgs` passes `--model`, `--effort` and `--advisor` for claude; the `starting` line, `current-<repo>.json` and a new `model` column at the end of `runs.tsv` say what ran; `scripts/measure-steps.py` groups by model; `docs/project/README.md` and `docs/technical/mc-run.md` describe it; the suite is green.
instruction: Read `sessionSettings` (`src/mc/run-plan.js` about line 786, `DEFAULT_MODEL = 'opus'` at line 33), `validateRunner` and the key lists in `src/mc/plan-schema.js` (`RUNNER_KEYS` line 80, `STEP_KEYS` line 60, `MODEL_RE` line 37), `modelArgs` in `src/adapters/claude-code.js` (line 237, `['--model', model]`), the two call sites in `src/mc/run.js` (`sessionSettings(plan?.plan?.runner || {})` at line 1721 for a step, `sessionSettings({})` at line 993 for a repair), and the tests `sessionSettings` and `headlessArgs` in `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` (lines 319 and 256) and `tests/mc/plan-schema.test.js`.

Flags, confirmed 2026-09-11 on claude 2.1.268: `--model <alias|name>`, `--effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max>` (both in `claude --help`), and `--advisor <model>`, which `--help` does not list but the documentation at code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor.md names as the per-session flag; it was accepted on a one-turn `claude -p` that day. A sonnet 5 main accepts `fable`, `opus` or `sonnet` as advisor; `opus` main accepts `fable` and `opus`; `haiku` cannot advise. The advisor is off unless asked for. The machine's `~/.claude/settings.json` sets `model: claude-fable-5-1[1m]` and `effortLevel: high`, which is why every runner session so far ran opus at high effort: `--model opus` overrode the first and nothing overrode the second.

Schema. `RUNNER_KEYS` gains `effort` and `advisor`. `effort` is one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; `advisor` matches `MODEL_RE` or is the string `off`. `STEP_KEYS` gains `runner`, validated by the same function but allowing only `model`, `effort`, `advisor` — `tool` and the interval keys are the plan's (say so in the problem text: `steps[i].runner.tool: a plan-level key`). Export the effort list so `run-plan.js` and the docs read the same one.

The boundary: a step's `runner` is the author's. `unauthorisedChanges` (plan-schema.js line 352) skips the session's own step entirely (`if (i === index) continue`) and then trusts the step role's prose for `status`/`pr`/`comments`. Tighten that one index: compare `from[index]` and `to[index]` on every key except `status`, `pr`, `comments`, `blocked_by`, and report `steps[i].<key>: a step session does not change it` — which covers `runner`, `title`, `done_when` and `instruction` at once. Read the test for `unauthorisedChanges` in `tests/mc/plan-schema.test.js` first: a session that only ticks `met` and writes its own three fields must still pass, and a session that resolved a plan conflict (run.test.js line 689) must still be judged against main's copy as it is today.

Resolution. `sessionSettings(planRunner, stepRunner, { kind })` returns `{ tool, model, effort, advisor, ... }`: step over plan over the defaults for that kind — step: `sonnet`, `medium`, `opus`; repair: `opus`, no effort, no advisor. `advisor: 'off'` anywhere means no flag. As today, a tool that is not claude gets no model default and now no effort or advisor either. Keep the interval field the function already returns (`budgetMinutes` today; step 3 renames it) untouched so the two steps do not fight over one line.

Arguments. `headlessArgs` takes `effort` and `advisor` beside `model` and, for claude only, appends `--effort <level>` and `--advisor <model>` when set. Put the two argument builders in `src/adapters/claude-code.js` beside `modelArgs` (`effortArgs`, `advisorArgs`) so `mc work` can use them later, and have `headlessArgs` call them through the adapter the way it calls `modelArgs`. Codex gets none of the three flags.

What ran. The `starting` line in `run.js` (lines 1006 and 1755) says `(claude sonnet · effort medium · advisor opus, …)`. `current-<repo>.json` (line 1764) carries `effort` and `advisor` beside `model`. `RUNS_HEADER` in `run-plan.js` line 31 gains `model` at the end, after `land_seconds`, and `tsvRow` writes the resolved model alias (`sonnet`, `opus`) there; every reader keys rows by the header (`brief-collect.js` line 319, `measure-steps.py`) so old rows read `undefined`/missing for the new column and nothing else moves. Do not insert a column anywhere but the end; `close-workarea.js` and `archive-plan.js` read rows by position in places — check them.

Measurement. `scripts/measure-steps.py` reads each session's json, which has `modelUsage` keyed by full model id (seen 2026-09-11: `claude-opus-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`). Add a `--by-model` grouping (or always print it): the cost, turns, wall, API-time and context-per-turn rows once per main model, where the main model is the `modelUsage` key with the most output tokens. This is the comparison the plan is measured on.

Docs. `docs/project/README.md` § *The overall part*, the `runner` bullet: the new keys, and that a step may carry `runner` with the three model keys. `docs/technical/mc-run.md` around line 493 (*Fresh, headless, and assembled from the plan's own frontmatter*): the resolution order, the defaults per kind, the three flags, and one sentence on why: opus at high on every turn was the cost, and the advisor is the strong model at decision points rather than throughout. Cite ruling 18 by name.

Tests: `sessionSettings` for step defaults, repair defaults, plan override, step override, `advisor: 'off'`, and codex getting nothing; `headlessArgs` for the three flags; schema tests for each new key and each refusal; `unauthorisedChanges` for a changed `runner` and a changed `instruction` on the session's own step. Run `npm test` once at the end, in the foreground.

steps.title: A check-in message replaces the budget kill, and only a stalled session is killed
comments: Blocked before any code, by the instruction's own gate: memoro's `origin/main` (8af3901) carries `runner.budget_minutes` in 14 plans, and in every one of them it is the whole `runner` object. `docs/project/language-voice/language-voice-do-alarms/PLAN.json` (150), `docs/project/msr-core/items-sweep/PLAN.json` (180), `docs/project/voice-chat/voice-audio-path/PLAN.json` (150), `docs/project/voice-chat/voice-session-report/PLAN.json` (150), and under `docs/project/sql-readiness/`: `sql-goal1-certification` (150), `sql-w1-universe-closure` (150), `sql-w2-search-closure` (120), `sql-w3-email-closure` (150), `sql-w4-automation-closure` (150), `sql-w5-relationship-closure` (150), `sql-w6-background-closure` (150), `sql-w7-operations-closure` (150), `sql-w9-account-closure` (150), `sql-w10-product-domains-closure` (150). Memoro's `docs/project/README.md:77` lists `budget_minutes` among the runner keys too. No memoro code reads the key; the grep outside the plans hits only that README line. Several of these plans have `ready` steps, so a schema that refuses the key stops them the round this step lands.

Recommendation for `step-cost-memoro-budget`: one docs-only memoro PR, landed before this step, that deletes the `runner` object from those 14 plans (it holds nothing else, and `runner` is optional, so dropping it is cleaner than leaving `{}`) and removes `budget_minutes` from memoro's `docs/project/README.md:77`. Then this step goes `ready` as written. Keeping the key accepted-but-ignored would break the contract's rule that every key the schema accepts is one the runner reads. In memoro-cli no plan on main carries the key: `runner-next-step` was archived in c781481, which removes the directory, so the schema never reads archived plans and the grep only needs the live tree; `step-cost`'s own plan mentions it only in prose.

Stream-json proven live, so build on stdin, not the `--resume` fallback. Claude 2.1.269, `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --model haiku --effort low` in a scratch directory. (a) A user message written after a `result` starts a new turn with its own `result`; the process stays alive on open stdin after a result and exits when stdin closes. (b) A user message written mid-turn is not dropped: the transcript shows a `queue-operation` enqueue/remove and the message is folded into the running turn as an `attachment` of type `queued_command`, not as a plain `user` entry. The turn still ends in one `result` (`queued_turn_count: 0`). Delivery and compliance are separate: in one run haiku-at-low saw the message and did not act on it, in another it answered it inside the same result. That is model behaviour, not an unreliable pipe. The live check of success criterion 2 therefore has to look for the `queued_command` attachment, not only a `user` line.

One process can emit more than one `result` line, and each carries its own `num_turns`, `usage` and `total_cost_usd` for that turn group, not a running total (one run: two results, `num_turns` 2 each). The instruction's rule of taking the last line that parses as a result undercounts `runs.tsv` whenever a check-in write races the session's own finish, and closing stdin on the first `result` can still race a check-in written just before it. That needs a choice the plan does not make: sum across results, or stop writing check-ins once a result is seen. Result line keys seen: `type`, `subtype`, `is_error`, `result`, `session_id`, `num_turns`, `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `modelUsage`, `permission_denials`, `stop_reason`, `terminal_reason`, `queued_turn_count`, `result_index`, `api_error_status`, `uuid`, plus timing fields (`ttft_ms`, `ttft_stream_ms`, `time_to_request_ms`, `first_content_frame_ms`, `fast_mode_*`, `subagent_stats`).
steps.done_when: `deps.session` in `src/mc/run.js` runs claude with `--input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose`, writes the prompt as the first user message on stdin, writes the check-in message every `check_in_minutes` while the session runs, closes stdin when the `result` event arrives, and kills the child only after `stall_minutes` without a byte on stdout; `readSessionOutput` reads the `result` line; `budget_minutes` is gone from the schema and from every plan on main, `check_in_minutes` and `stall_minutes` replace it; the page's clock shows elapsed time and check-ins and no *over budget*; `docs/technical/mc-run.md` and `docs/project/README.md` say so; the suite is green.
instruction: Read `deps.session` in `src/mc/run.js` (lines 205–249: `spawn` with `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']`, `timeout: timeoutMs`, `killSignal: 'SIGTERM'`, and the `close` handler that maps a SIGTERM with no status to `TIMEOUT_EXIT`), both call sites (`runProject` about line 1780 with `timeoutMs: settings.budgetMinutes * 60_000`, the repair at line 1012), `readSessionOutput` in `src/mc/run-plan.js` (about line 700, `JSON.parse(stdout)` of the whole output), `sessionSettings` and `DEFAULT_BUDGET_MINUTES` (line 35), the tests at `tests/mc/run.test.js` line 915 (*a timed-out session is logged as timeout with exit 142*) and 1027 (*a session that timed out with its pull request open is held too*), `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` line 270, and the page's clock: `status-collect.js` lines 299–313 (`budget_seconds`, `over_budget`) and `page-render.js` lines 271–276 and 438–442. `docs/technical/mc-run.md` describes the kill at lines 501, 731, 929–935.

What is proven and what is not, as of 2026-09-11 on claude 2.1.268. Proven with a one-turn run: `claude -p --output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json --verbose` with one `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"…"}}` line on stdin answers that message, ignores the positional prompt (it answered the stdin message and not the `-p` one), streams `system`, `assistant` and `rate_limit_event` lines, and ends with one `{"type":"result", …}` line carrying the same fields the json format carried — `session_id`, `num_turns`, `subtype`, `is_error`, `result`, `usage`, `total_cost_usd`, `modelUsage`. Not proven: that a second user message written to stdin while the model is mid-turn is delivered after that turn rather than dropped, and that the process stays alive waiting for stdin after its first `result`. Prove both first, in a scratch directory with `--model haiku --effort low`, before wiring anything: send a message that takes a few turns (a small file-reading task), write a second message during it, and read the transcript order in the output. If the second message is dropped, the fallback is `--resume <session_id>` with the check-in as the new prompt after a clean stop — say which of the two you built and why in the PR.

Session shape. `deps.session({ bin, args, cwd, prompt, checkInMs, stallMs, checkIn })`: stdin is a pipe; the prompt goes in as the first stream-json user message and is removed from `headlessArgs`' positional (`-p` stays, the prompt does not, for claude; codex keeps its positional and its `exec --json`, and gets neither check-in nor stall guard — its stdin stays `ignore`). Every `checkInMs`, if the child is still running, write `checkIn(elapsedMinutes, count)` as a user message and count it. On each stdout chunk reset the stall timer; when it fires, SIGTERM the child and mark `stalled: true`. When a line with `"type":"result"` arrives, end stdin (`child.stdin.end()`), and let `close` resolve as today. The 256 MiB cap on collected output stays. Remove the `timeout` option from `spawn`.

The check-in text, in `src/mc/run-plan.js` as `checkInPrompt({ minutes, count })`, plain and short: you have been running for N minutes (this is check-in number K); judge whether this step can be finished in this session. If it can, say so in one line and go on — no other answer is needed. If it cannot — you are going in circles, a test cannot be made green, the plan does not match the code — commit what you have, set your step `blocked` with `blocked_by: { "kind": "decision", "name": "<project>-check-in" }` and in `comments` what you found and what the next session should do differently, open the pull request, and stop. Do not start anything new after a check-in that says it cannot be finished. Name the project so the blocker name is a name (`NAME_RE` in plan-schema.js).
